aria: Animated recap of the Bucks' 116 to 111 road win over the Raptors: Tyler Herro's 3-pointer with 1:03 left that made it 116 to 106, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Herro's 32 points, the top scorers, how the Bucks won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Bucks' 116–111 win at Toronto on Nov 23, 2026, from the Covers box score; all 116 Milwaukee points and all 111 Toronto points add up from the player lines, and the shooting totals (41 of 81, 14 of 28 from three, 20 of 24 FT for Milwaukee; 41 of 95, 14 of 38, 15 of 22 for Toronto), rebounds (44–44; offensive 7–15), blocks (9–7), steals (4–9), points in the paint (52–44), fast-break points (6–15) and the biggest leads (10 each) are from Covers. The quarter scores (28–21–36–31 to 28–25–27–31) add up to both totals; the Raptors' 53–49 halftime lead is also in Brew Hoop, and the Bucks' 85–80 lead after three is in the AP. Herro's 3 first-half points, 15 in the third (AP; TSN/Canadian Press) and 14 in the fourth (Field Level Media) add up to his 32. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

The win ended Milwaukee's 13-game losing streak, the second-longest in franchise history (AP), and was its first since Oct. 26 against Indiana (TSN/Canadian Press). Herro scored a career-high 50 in Saturday's loss at Philadelphia (AP; Field Level Media). Myles Turner and Jakob Poeltl fouled out (AP). Toronto played without Kawhi Leonard (left knee) and RJ Barrett (hamstring) (AP; TSN/Canadian Press) and lost for the seventh time in eight games (AP; Field Level Media). Next: the Bucks host Brooklyn on Wednesday, the Raptors host Brooklyn on Friday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Tyler Herro's 3-pointer with 1:03 left: Field Level Media: "Herro later splashed a triple to give the Bucks a 116-106 lead with 1:03 left." It was the Bucks' biggest lead (10, Covers) and, with Milwaukee finishing on 116, its last points. The board's Bucks +7 to +10 follows from the three. The shot isn't described further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Milwaukee Bucks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Herro's listed 6-foot-5 and 195 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-3.25 wingspan from the 2019 draft combine (247Sports, NBADraft.net), in the Bucks' road kit with No. 11 (Wikipedia) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
